claim_boundary.supports: Kernel-checked for Finsets of any type with decidable equality: D subset of W and (W minus D) disjoint from B imply |(W minus D) union B| = |W| - |D| + |B|; with no hypothesis |next| = |W| - |W cap D| + |B| - |(W minus D) cap B| (card_next_exact), so the integer identity holds if and only if |D minus W| = |(W minus D) cap B| (formula_iff); explicit counterexamples when D subset W is dropped and when disjointness is dropped, an explicit agreement with both dropped (exact cancellation), and an explicit case where the truncated natural-number identity holds although D is not inside W; every pair of counts (s, s2) is the count pair of an admissible step, and two admissible splits give the same counts, so a count sequence is not a law; the list-length reading of the source needs no disjointness, while for duplicate-free inputs the filter-based list register is duplicate-free exactly when the births avoid the survivors (list_register_nodup_iff). Exactly one violated hypothesis never permits the integer identity (single_violation_fails; its disjointness-alone half is the corollary of formula_iff with D inside W). The anchors fails_without_subset, fails_without_disjoint, holds_accidentally_without_hypotheses, nat_truncation_masks_subset_violation, split_not_determined and list_overlap_not_nodup are single instances, not universal statements. Axioms of the Finset theorems: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound (standard Mathlib); the list theorems use propext and Quot.sound or less. Native: exhaustive classification of all 8^u triples (W, D, B) of subsets for u = 0..5 into the four hypothesis classes with, per class, the number of triples for which the integer and the truncated identity hold, four count sequences (including the source displayed sequence 0,1,1,1,0,1,1) with their exact number of admissible (|D|, |B|) splits per step, and two exhaustive list-register censuses (alphabet 2 with lists up to length 2, alphabet 3 up to length 3) showing the length identity holds for every triple and that duplicate-free inputs give a duplicate-free register exactly when the births avoid the survivors.
claim_boundary.does_not_support: Which demands an engine actually carries; any claim that the displayed survivor sequence (0,1,1,1,0,1,1) is a native or universal law (the source itself calls it a chosen ledger example); the preservation.py demand_step frozenset reading and any Python or Rust wrapper over it; multiset or ordered-log registers as a state beyond the filter-based list register of Paper.lean (the erase-based removeAll register of Paper001.lean is not re-proved, and the Nodup conjunct of that List Nat statement is only matched by the filter-based list_register_nodup_iff and the native census); the identification of the active count s_n with the cumulative history |H_n|; universes of more than five elements; any physical or thermodynamic interpretation.
claim_boundary.narrowest_claim: For finite sets, |(W minus D) union B| = |W| - |D| + |B| holds when D is inside W and the births avoid W minus D (births may coincide with discharged elements), it fails whenever exactly one of the two hypotheses is violated; when both are violated it holds if and only if |D minus W| = |(W minus D) cap B| (exact cancellation); and it imposes no constraint on a sequence of counts.
claim_boundary.next_test: Supply the missing count wrapper over preservation.demand_step of the opened preservation.py: show that the frozenset next-active set it returns equals the Finset (W minus D) union B of this model, carry the two hypotheses as typed fields of the wrapper, and replay the identity on the wrapper actual outputs.

earlier_pass.notes: Lean module lean4/DemandAccounting.lean (sha identical to p1/construction copy) recompiles exit 0 under v4.35.0. Statement fidelity is good: demand_accounting is stated for arbitrary Finset over a DecidableEq type with exactly hypotheses D subset W and Disjoint (W \ D) B; card_next_exact and formula_iff are genuine unconditional integer statements (no truncation); fails_of_excess_without_overlap is a universal statement; the three boundary theorems and nat_truncation_masks_subset_violation are explicitly existential instances (and are described as such in the module docstring, though the profile 'supports' prose says 'explicit counterexamples', which is accurate). Weak points. (a) narrowest_claim says the identity 'fails when either hypothesis is dropped except under exact cancellation'. That is imprecise: dropping ONE hypothesis never permits the identity (subset dropped alone: fails_of_excess_without_overlap; disjointness dropped alone: follows from formula_iff because D subset W gives |D\W|=0, but this is NOT a named Lean theorem, only the existential fails_without_disjoint plus native class counts for u<=5 where class 'overlap_violated_only' has 0 holding triples). Cancellation needs BOTH hypotheses violated. The universal 'disjointness alone fails' is therefore backed by a one-line corollary nobody stated, not by an anchor. (b) list_overlap_not_nodup is a single decide-instance, so 'the Nodup conjunct needs disjointness' is shown only as non-redundancy of that hypothesis on one instance; the positive Nodup statement of Paper001.lean is not re-proved here. (c) The 'decompositions' field counts cardinality pairs (d,b), not (D,B) set pairs; the profile says 'admissible (d, b) splits' which is correct but the closed form s+1-max(0,s-t) used by the checker is the same arithmetic as the producer's loop (only realizability is searched), so the sequence records are weakly independent. every_step_is_an_accounting makes 'realized' always true, so the flag carries no information beyond the theorem and the sequence_step_unrealizable mutant is effectively a flipped flag. (d) The profile's second ledger claim 'class sizes' exact cross-checks are strong: the DP over (|W|,|D|,|B|,|D\W|,|(W\D)&B|) is a genuinely different algorithm from the bitmask triple loop, and tallies are verified including the truncated-identity column. Checker is order-insensitive only through sorted public-case keys, which is fine; no tolerance, all ints type-checked (bool excluded). Mutants: seven semantic near misses are leaf-count edits but each corresponds to a real misreading (subset/disjointness dropped, natural subtraction, accidental agreement, sequence as law); missing near miss: births coinciding with DISCHARGED elements (allowed) read as a violation, i.e. disjointness taken against W or D rather than W\D, which is exactly the Paper001.lean hdisj subtlety the profile highlights; also a multiset/log register where multiplicity makes the identity hold without disjointness (the list_length reading) has no mutant. next_test is the node's own missing wrapper obligation (the cited derivation tfq_0369 lists exactly this 'missing obligation: a count wrapper around demand_step'); it is not boilerplate and differs from does_not_support (which lists the wrapper only as an exclusion). I could not locate preservation.py in the repo, so that wrapper remains an unopened source. Axioms: all Finset theorems use propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound (Mathlib standard); the profile does not mention Classical.choice for this node, harmless but worth one clause.
